title: AI-Enhanced Spectral CT Image Reconstruction for Improved Detection of Abnormal Findings, Diagnostic Confidence and Reading Workflows
summary:
Computed tomography is an X-ray technique that produces detailed cross-sectional images of the inside of the body. A newer form, called spectral computed tomography, also measures how strongly different tissues absorb X-rays of different energies. This makes it possible to create special images on which tumors, changes in blood vessels or inflammation are often easier to see. One drawback is that these images are often very “noisy”, meaning they look grainy and uneven and therefore appear blurry. This makes them harder to assess and limits their use in everyday clinical practice.
A new method has recently become available that uses artificial intelligence to greatly reduce this image noise without losing fine details. This study will examine whether images created with artificial intelligence have better image quality than the images used so far, and whether radiologists can detect abnormal findings on them more easily and with greater confidence. It will also examine whether the method could help reduce radiation exposure and the amount of contrast agent for patients in the future.
To do this, examinations of about 150 adult patients will be analyzed retrospectively. These patients had such an examination as part of their regular care at Heidelberg University Hospital between July 2025 and March 2026. No additional examinations will be performed for the study, and patient care will not be affected. Using the existing measurement data, images will be created afterwards with the new method and compared with the previous images from the same examination. On the one hand, image quality will be determined objectively based on measurements taken in the images. In addition, several radiologists will assess the images without knowing which method was used to create them. All data will be analyzed without names and only within the hospital.
conditions: Patients undergoing clinically indicated diagnostic spectral computed tomography for heterogeneous indications in routine and emergency care (including, among others, oncologic, cardiovascular, and inflammatory diseases); not restricted to any specific disease.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults (≥ 18 years) who underwent a diagnostic CT examination on a dual-layer detector spectral CT scanner (Philips Spectral CT 7500) as part of their routine or emergency medical care at Diagnostic and Interventional Radiology, Heidelberg University Hospital, between 01 July 2025 and 31 March 2026.
Exclusion criteria:
(1) Lack of spectral raw data. 
(2) Imaging data that are incomplete or of insufficient quality (e.g., due to premature termination of the examination, delayed or failed injection of intravenous contrast medium, or severe motion artifacts).
